notes.title: Start here: an education ops app after its twenty-story backlog
notes.body:
This repo is Agentic Education Operations, a Next.js and Prisma modular monolith for running a school: students, sections, assignments, attendance, interventions and nine deterministic agents. The `fabledocs/` folder is the guide this pack uses.

Read in this order:

1. `fabledocs/01-app-overview.md` sections 4 (the layering rule), 6 (the four flows) and 8 (the agent framework).
2. `fabledocs/03-progress.md`, which says what each of the twenty stories actually shipped and which criteria were left partial.
3. The stories in `fabledocs/02-user-stories.md` that the quizzes draw on: US-05, US-06, US-07, US-10, US-11, US-15, US-16, US-17 and US-18.

Every decision lives in `packages/domain` (or `packages/agents`) as a pure function, and every write goes through an application service. So for each story, find the pure function first, then the service that calls it. The quizzes give you a concrete input and ask what the function returns: trace it by hand.

notes.title: The teaching loop: queue order, grade maths, attendance
notes.body:
Three domain files carry the teaching-loop stories.

- `packages/domain/src/workload.ts` holds `rankGradingQueue` (US-05). Read the `RISK_URGENCY` table and the sort comparator, including every tie-breaker, before working any example.
- `packages/domain/src/grades.ts` holds `calculateGradeSummary` and its weighted sibling (US-06, US-15). List each submission status and note which of the two totals (earned, possible) it touches. The long comments explain why each status is treated the way it is. In the weighted version, look at what happens to a period with nothing scored.
- `packages/domain/src/attendance.ts` holds `findLongestAbsenceStreak` and `canRecordAttendance` (US-07). The streak function has two paths, chosen by whether `sessionDates` is passed; read both loops and compare what each one iterates over. `canRecordAttendance` is a list of early refusals: note each condition and its threshold.

`packages/domain/src/enrollment.ts` (US-10) follows the same shape for waitlist promotion: a decision function that re-checks things at write time.

notes.title: Reports, the job queue and the agent platform
notes.body:
The later stories add infrastructure around the domain.

- **Reports (US-16).** `packages/domain/src/reports.ts` builds a snapshot payload, diffs two snapshots into named buckets, and derives an idempotency key from an ISO week. Read the comment on `isoWeek` about the new-year edge, and check which bucket each kind of student lands in. CSV export lives in `packages/shared/src/index.ts` (`escapeCsvValue`): read the two regular expressions in order.
- **Jobs (US-11).** `jobService.enqueue` in `packages/application/src/services/job-service.ts` is the only producer. Note which existing statuses make it return early.
- **Agent manifests (US-17).** `packages/domain/src/versions.ts` compares versions; `manifest-gate.ts` runs three checks before any agent executes. Compare its permission check with the role branches in `permissions.ts`.
- **Sub-agents (US-18).** `confidenceFromSubagents` in `packages/agents/src/helpers.ts` turns child confidences into a penalty. Read how the penalty is sized.

notes.title: Urgency first, then days waiting
notes.body:
`rankGradingQueue` scores each item as days waiting plus `RISK_URGENCY`: Critical 2 + 14 = 16, High 8 + 7 = 15, Medium 12 + 3 = 15, Low 9 + 0 = 9. The comparator sorts by urgency, then by `daysWaiting` (descending), then by id. High and Medium tie at 15, and Medium has waited longer, so it is second.

- *High waiting 8 days* is third: same urgency as Medium, fewer days waiting.
- *Low waiting 9 days* is last; a Low-risk item gets no weight at all.
- *Critical waiting 2 days* is first, not second: that is the point of the risk weight.

notes.title: Which statuses reach the denominator
notes.body:
`calculateGradeSummary` adds a Missing record's points to `possiblePoints` with nothing earned. A scored record adds both. Since US-06, a Late record with no score also adds its points to the denominator. A Submitted record with no score adds nothing, on purpose: work the teacher has not reached is not failed. So earned is 90 and possible is 100 + 100 + 50 = 250, giving 36%.

- *90%* is the old behaviour where only graded work counted; Missing always counted, so it was never 90%.
- *60%* (90 / 150) drops the Late submission, which is the bug US-06 fixed.
- *About 25.7%* (90 / 350) also penalises the Submitted, ungraded work.

notes.title: An empty period is dropped, not zeroed
notes.body:
P2 holds only NotStarted work, so its own summary has no possible points and a null average. `calculateWeightedGradeSummary` keeps only periods with a non-null average and a positive weight, then divides by their total weight. Only P1 remains: 80 * 0.4 / 0.4 = 80.

- *32* treats P2 as zero; the comment calls that the single most alarming thing a gradebook can do.
- *null* would only happen with no scored work in any weighted period, and even then it falls back to the flat average.
- *56* invents a 40% score for P2; nothing in the code assigns a value to an empty period.

excerpts.quote: const scored = periods.filter((period) => period.average !== null && period.weight > 0);

notes.title: Walking the schedule instead of the records
notes.body:
With no `sessionDates`, `findLongestAbsenceStreak` walks the sorted records: Absent, Absent, Absent, so 3. With sessions, it walks the schedule and looks each day up. Wednesday has no record, and anything other than Absent (including no record at all) resets the run. So Monday gives 1, Wednesday resets to 0, then Friday and Monday give 2.

- *3 both ways* ignores the reset on the unrecorded Wednesday.
- *2 both ways* forgets that the record-only path never sees Wednesday.
- *4 with sessions* would count the missing record as an absence, which the comment rejects.

notes.title: Enrolled only, and a day of slack
notes.body:
`canRecordAttendance` refuses unless `enrollmentStatus` is exactly "Enrolled", so the Waitlisted student is refused at the first check. For the Enrolled student the section is Active, the date is inside the term, and the future check only refuses dates more than 24 hours ahead. Twenty hours is within that slack.

- *Both refused* is wrong: the code allows up to a day in advance.
- *Both allowed* is wrong: a waitlist place is not a seat.
- *Waitlisted allowed* reverses both decisions.

notes.title: Promotion re-checks eligibility before capacity
notes.body:
`decideWaitlistPromotion` first requires the row to be Waitlisted, then refuses a Withdrawn or Graduated student, then checks the section, the teacher and capacity. A Withdrawn student is refused with "Student is no longer eligible for enrollment." even though a seat is open.

- *Allowed because a seat is open* skips the eligibility check that runs first.
- *Still at capacity* is the reason for a full section; here a seat opened.
- *Set back to active* is exactly what the comment says the check prevents: re-activating a record the office closed.

notes.title: Prefix first, then quote
notes.body:
`escapeCsvValue` runs two steps. If the text starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR, it is prefixed with an apostrophe. Then, if it contains a comma, quote or newline, it is wrapped in double quotes with inner quotes doubled. `=SUM(A1,B1)` gets both: apostrophe, then quotes because of the comma. `-5` becomes the string "-5", gets the apostrophe, and has no comma.

- *Quotes only, -5 unchanged* skips the defusal; the comment says negative numbers get the prefix on purpose.
- *Apostrophe with no quotes* forgets the comma rule.
- *Quoting "-5"* would need a comma, quote or newline in it.

notes.title: A first appearance is an addition, not an escalation
notes.body:
In `diffReports`, each current row is looked up in the previous snapshot. When there is no previous row, the student is pushed to `added` and the loop `continue`s, so the elevation checks and the movers list never see her. Her entry's delta is null anyway.

- *newlyElevated* needs a previous level outside High/Critical; she had none.
- *Both buckets* cannot happen, because of the `continue`.
- *biggestMovers with a delta from zero*: delta is null for a missing side, and null deltas are filtered out of movers.

notes.title: The Thursday decides the ISO year
notes.body:
`weeklyReportKey` writes `school` for a null scope, then `isoWeek(date)`. `isoWeek` moves the date to the Thursday of its week and uses that Thursday's year. Friday 1 January 2027 sits in the week whose Thursday is 31 December 2026. 2026 began on a Thursday, so it has 53 ISO weeks, and this is week 53.

- *2027-W01* is the naive calendar-year answer the comment warns about; week 1 of 2027 starts on Monday 4 January.
- *null in the key* ignores the `?? "school"` fallback.
- *W00* is not an ISO week number; the format starts at W01.

excerpts.quote: Thursday determines the year an ISO week belongs to.

notes.title: Only in-flight work is deduplicated
notes.body:
`enqueue` looks up the key. It returns the existing row only when that row is Queued, Running or Retrying. A Succeeded job is finished history, so a new Queued job is created, and because the old row still holds the key, the new one is stored as the key plus `:` and `Date.now()`.

- *Returned unchanged* is the in-flight case, not this one.
- *Unique-constraint error* is exactly what the suffix avoids.
- *Reset to Queued* would rewrite history; the code never updates the old row.

notes.title: Numeric compare, inactive rows filtered first
notes.body:
`selectActiveVersion` filters to active rows before comparing, so 2.0.0 is out. `compareSemver` compares the numeric cores: 1.0.10 beats 1.0.9 because 10 > 9 as numbers. For equal cores, a version with no pre-release suffix outranks one with a suffix, so 1.0.10 beats 1.0.10-beta.1.

- *2.0.0* is inactive; deactivating it is how an operator rolls back.
- *1.0.9* is what a plain string compare would choose.
- *1.0.10-beta.1* loses to the release of the same core, per semver.

notes.title: Manifest permissions add to agent:run
notes.body:
`resolveManifest` loops over the manifest's `requiredPermissions` and calls `assertCan` for each. The Teacher branch of `canPerform` grants `agent:run` (and grading, attendance and assignment actions for their own sections), but not `notification:manage`, so the second check throws and the run never starts.

- *agent:run is enough* is the pre-US-17 behaviour; now the manifest's list is checked in addition.
- *Own students only* describes no rule here; the refusal is about a missing permission.
- *Recorded as Failed* is what the gate avoids: it throws before an AgentRun row is written.

notes.title: Half the gap to the weakest child
notes.body:
`confidenceFromSubagents(85, [90, 60, 80])` takes the minimum child, 60. It is below the base, so the penalty is (85 - 60) / 2 = 12.5, and `Math.round(72.5)` gives 73.

- *77, the mean* is ruled out: the comment says averaging lets confident children hide a weak one.
- *60* would cap the parent at the weakest child; the penalty is half the gap, not all of it.
- *85* would ignore the weak child; a child at or above the base costs nothing, but 60 is below it.
